findings.finding: My own GAP-ENTITY_COVERAGE-008 CLOSED_DERIVED was wrong: two documented deity predicates disagree on 29 of 214 nodes
findings.evidence: Live Neo4j, READ session, 2026-09-17. The predicate the API actually runs is src/vedagraph/api/services/deity_population.py:deity_structure_clause, filtering on `structure` against DEITY_STRUCTURES={ABSTRACT,GROUP,INDIVIDUAL,PAIR} and NON_DEITY_STRUCTURES={HUMAN,PATRON_PRAISE,UNSPECIFIED}: it excludes 30 and admits 184. The predicate the eligibility contract wrote is deity_eligibility_ruling / is_deity: 57 NOT_DEITY, 157 admitted. Cross-tabulated, the disagreement is exactly 29 rows: 28 ABSTRACT nodes ruled NOT_DEITY with non_deity_kind ABSTRACTION_NOT_AN_ADDRESSEE are nevertheless ADMITTED to the served population because ABSTRACT is in DEITY_STRUCTURES, and 1 UNSPECIFIED node ruled DEITY is EXCLUDED. Clause 1 of the entry's test ('derivable by ONE documented predicate') therefore fails; clause 3 ('the ABSTRACT decision recorded ... rather than applied implicitly') is recorded and not applied, since all 42 ABSTRACT rows carry basis ABSTRACT_LABEL_RULING and the served population honours none of it. Clause 2's '29 non-deities' has four competing referents: the test says 29, the live filter excludes 30, deity_population.py's own caveat says '30 of the 214 are not gods ... and one dog. This response excludes all 30', and the eligibility contract identifies 57.
findings.verdict: MY ERROR. The R1 gate asked 'deity_eligibility_ruling IS NULL -> 0', which measures that the field is POPULATED and never that it is CONSUMED -- the exact 'validator that silently skips / measure coverage, not just precision' trap I cited in my own receipt. Product consequence: clients receive 28 abstractions the eligibility ruling says are not addressees, and GAP-ENTITY_COVERAGE-002's materialisation denominator is 152 or 184 depending on which predicate it reads.
findings.fixed_and_reaudited: REVERTED to STILL_IMPLEMENTATION_FIXABLE at the generator, with a replacement gate that measures the two predicates against each other (expect 29, closed state 0). Re-ran the audit and --write; drift 0, fixable 43->20.

findings.finding: My Phase 6 renderer split strings at hyphens, corrupting 19 evidence strings including an unfollowable citation path and three gap IDs
findings.evidence: textwrap.wrap(break_long_words=False) still breaks on hyphens, and each wrapped line was emitted as a literal ending in a space. Detected by regex [A-Za-z0-9_]- [A-Za-z0-9_] over every RULINGS string: 15 in basis/citation/reaudit plus 4 in the blocked-evidence dicts. The worst was GAP-ATTRIBUTION-WHITNEY-UNRESOLVED-OBJECT-001's CLOSED_SCOPE_DECISION citation, which read 'docs/reports/data- completeness/OWNER_DECISIONS.md:589-600' -- a path no reader can open, in the one field the status guard exists to protect. Also corrupted: 'GAP- ATTRIBUTION-004', 'GAP- MORPHOLOGY-005', 'GAP- ATTRIBUTION-002' (gap ids a grep will not find), and 'pratika- keyed', 'search- normalised', 'multi- word', 'per- epithet', 'MIS- GRAINED', 'sacred- texts.com', 'rights- compatible', 'arcika- verse', 'range- covered', 'mantras- reached', 'pair- scope'.
findings.verdict: MY ERROR, in a durable evidence artifact. My own new citation gate did not catch it because the same citation string also named one intact path, and the gate used any() over the paths.
findings.fixed_and_reaudited: Fixed the renderer (break_on_hyphens=False) and re-rendered all 46 authored rulings from their source text plus 4 literal boundaries in the evidence dicts. Re-verified: 0 remaining artifacts, every CLOSED_SCOPE_DECISION citation path now resolves on disk, statuses unchanged, audit re-run and re-written, drift 0.
